plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: Trees covered in clouds of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers. The blossoms carpet streets and gardens in violet as they fall.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer in the Southern Hemisphere, roughly October to December
plants.location: Pretoria, South Africa, and across southern Africa, Australia and South America
plants.funFact: Jacaranda is native to South America but is now planted in warm regions worldwide. Pretoria is nicknamed the Jacaranda City because of its tens of thousands of trees.

plants.name: Chrysanthemum × morifolium
plants.description: A classic autumn favorite with dense, layered pompons and spidery petals. Its blooms keep a garden colorful when most other flowers have faded.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn in the Northern Hemisphere, typically September to November
plants.location: Japan, where the flowers are celebrated in autumn chrysanthemum festivals, and temperate gardens across the Northern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: Chrysanthemums are short-day plants. They set buds only when nights grow long enough, which is why they bloom in autumn.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: A glossy-leaved evergreen shrub that opens delicate, lightly fragrant flowers with golden stamens in the cool days of late autumn. The blooms often drop petals in soft drifts beneath the plant.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn to early winter, roughly October to December
plants.location: Southern Japan, its native range, and mild-climate gardens such as the southeastern United States
plants.funFact: Its seeds are pressed to make camellia oil, which has long been used in Japan for cooking and hair care. Sasanqua is also a close relative of the tea plant.
